as_written_in_papers.quote: Three novel variants were detected in Exon 4 of the ITGß2 gene; the missense variant c.185G > A was identified in P19 and P28, it caused a change of amino acid at position 62 from cysteine to tyrosine, which might lead to changes in the protein features.

cases.statement: 2 person(s) in PMID 38578558 (P19, P28); clinical data from Table 1, genotype from the Discussion and the Molecular Studies paragraph.

Three novel variants were detected in Exon 4 of the ITGß2 gene; the missense variant c.185G > A was identified in P19 and P28, it caused a change of amino acid at position 62 from cysteine to tyrosine, which might lead to changes in the protein features.
All patients showed homozygous phenotype except P1 (non-consanguineous parents) who showed a compound heterozygous phenotype (p.Gly284Ser and p.Glu668Glyfs*23).
Only 3 patients were LAD-I^−, and their CD18 level was barely above 2% (P28, P29, and P30).
All of them are alive, however, suffering from aggressive autoinflammatory symptoms in the form of periodontitis and enteropathy [4, 25, 26].

phenotype_specificity.statement: Per-person Table 1 rows show early-onset umbilical stump and/or skin and soft-tissue disease, as described for the cohort. CD18 deficiency is stated for all patients at cohort level only. No testing of other genes is reported.

| **P28** | ♀ | + | 1 ♀ (died-1 m-sepsis) | 0.4 | 2 | 1.6 | Yes | Yes | oral thrush, enteropathy | died (6 m ) |
Umbilical stump disease and/or skin and soft tissue disease were the first presenting symptoms in all patients included in this study, among many other studies [3, 13–18, 20–23].
By definition, CD18 and CD11b were deficient in all patients (0-4.4%, mean 0.9%; and 0-3.8%, mean 0.53%, respectively).

segregation.statement: No relative was genotyped for this variant. Table 1 lists deceased siblings with an LAD-like history for P19, P28; they were not tested.

quotes.quote: | **P19** | ♂ | + | 1 ♀ (died-7 m-pneumonia) | 1 | 2 | 1 | Yes | - | pneumonia, Oral thrush | lost to follow up |

Since the variants are segregated in an autosomal recessive manner, the findings will support genetic counselling for the families as well.

in_trans.statement: Reported homozygous (all patients homozygous except P1). Parental genotypes are not reported, so phase or homozygosity was not confirmed in parents.

functional.statement: No assay of the variant itself. Patient-cell flow cytometry: P28 is named among the three patients with moderate CD18 deficiency (CD18 'barely above 2%'); P19's value is not given (cohort: CD18 deficient in all).

quotes.quote: Only 3 patients were LAD-I^−, and their CD18 level was barely above 2% (P28, P29, and P30).
By definition, CD18 and CD11b were deficient in all patients (0-4.4%, mean 0.9%; and 0-3.8%, mean 0.53%, respectively).
Most of the patients (90.2%) had severe CD18 deficiency (< 2% expression), while a few others showed moderate deficiency, and there were no patients with mild deficiency (Fig. 1).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Cys62Tyr) (batch HGVS); paper: c.185G > A, exon 4.

quotes.quote: Three novel variants were detected in Exon 4 of the ITGß2 gene; the missense variant c.185G > A was identified in P19 and P28, it caused a change of amino acid at position 62 from cysteine to tyrosine, which might lead to changes in the protein features.
This variant has not previously been reported in LAD-I patients, although an adjacent missense variant c.184T > C; p.Cys62Arg was previously reported by Van De Vijver et al. in 2012 [37].
Most ITGß2 mutations lead to reduced/null expression of β2-integrins on the leukocyte surface [33].

population_data_in_papers.statement: Cohort-level only: the 10 variants the authors call novel were 'not found in ExAC nor1000G'. The paper does not list which 10 variants that sentence covers.

quotes.quote: Out of the 16 identified disease-causing variants; 6 were previously reported, while the remaining 10 were novel and were not found in ExAC nor1000G suggesting heterogeneity in the mutation spectrum for LAD-I.

authors_classification.statement: No per-variant ACMG classification is shown. The Methods say variants were categorised under ACMG guidelines, and the authors call all 16 variants 'disease-causing'.

quotes.quote: In our study, direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGß2 gene revealed 16 disease-causing variants in 28 patients.

The identified variants were categorized as pathogenic/likely pathogenic/variant of uncertain significance (VUS)/likely benign/benign based on American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines [9].

concerns: Zygosity rests on one cohort-wide sentence ('All patients showed homozygous phenotype except P1'); parental genotypes are not reported.
No per-person CD18 percentage is given; only cohort ranges and the three moderate-deficiency patients (P28, P29, P30) are named.

The paper says this patient's variant was previously reported by the same centre (ref 10, PMID 35482138), yet the Discussion calls the variant novel; the same patient is probably in that earlier paper, which is not in this batch.
The paper contradicts itself on P28: the Discussion says P28, P29 and P30 (the LAD-I^- patients) are all alive, but Table 1 gives P28's outcome as 'died (6 m )'.
P19 and P28 are different people (male and female). The paper does not say whether they are related; each has a deceased sibling.
P28 has moderate CD18 deficiency ('barely above 2%') with the same variant that P19 carries; P19's CD18 class is not stated per person.
notes_for_panel: Two carriers (P19 male, P28 female), both homozygous, both from consanguineous families with a sibling who died in infancy (untested). P28 is one of three LAD-I^- patients (CD18 barely above 2%). Note the alive/died contradiction for P28.
